name: Flamingo
intro: A flamingo is a tall pink bird. It wades in shallow water.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A flamingo is a tall pink bird.
It has very long, thin legs.
Its long neck can bend like the letter S.
Its beak bends down in the middle.
The biggest kind can be taller than a first grader.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Flamingos live in shallow water.
They live in lagoons and lakes.
Some of these lakes have salty water.
American flamingos live on islands in the Caribbean Sea.
Flamingos live together in big groups called colonies.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Flamingos eat shrimp, snails, and algae.
A flamingo puts its head upside down in the water.
Its beak works like a strainer to catch food.
Their pink color comes from the food they eat.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: Flamingo parents build a little hill of mud for a nest.
The mother lays one egg on top.
The egg hatches after about one month.
The chick is fluffy and gray or white.
It turns pink as it grows up.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A new chick is about the size of a tennis ball.
Parents feed their chick a kind of milk from their bodies.
Flamingos run on the water before they fly.
Flamingos hear well, but they can barely smell.
A flamingo can live for a very long time.

vocab.meaning: Tiny plant-like living things that grow in water.
A big group of animals that live together.
A shallow pool of salty water near the ocean.
